---
title: "MIT OpenCourseWare"
date: 2026-10-01
description: "Freely available MIT courses with lecture videos, assignments and notes."
---

All of these come with **lecture videos**, **assignments** and **notes**, which keeps me far more engaged than reading alone. Within each topic they run roughly from where I'd start to where I'd end up. All from [MIT OpenCourseWare](https://ocw.mit.edu/).

## Mathematics

- [Single Variable Calculus (18.01), David Jerison](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-01-single-variable-calculus-fall-2006/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A clear, no-nonsense rebuild of calculus from limits to integration. Almost everything else on this list leans on it.</details>
- [Linear Algebra (18.06), Gilbert Strang](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Strang teaches the geometry first and the machinery second, which is why it finally clicks. Essential for neural data analysis and deep learning alike.</details>
- [Learn Differential Equations, Gilbert Strang & Cleve Moler](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-18-009-learn-differential-equations-up-close-with-gilbert-strang-and-cleve-moler-fall-2015/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Short, focused videos on how differential equations describe real dynamics. A good bridge towards modelling neural and physical systems.</details>
- [Matrix Calculus for Machine Learning and Beyond (18.S096)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-s096-matrix-calculus-for-machine-learning-and-beyond-january-iap-2023/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Shows how to differentiate with vectors and matrices properly, so backpropagation and gradient-based fitting feel principled rather than magical.</details>
- [Mathematics for Computer Science (6.042J)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-042j-mathematics-for-computer-science-spring-2015/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Proofs, graphs, counting and probability in one course. It trains you to reason carefully and formally about discrete structures.</details>
- [Introduction to Probability (RES.6-012), John Tsitsiklis](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/pages/part-i-the-fundamentals/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Concise lectures that build probability from the fundamentals. A solid base for the Bayesian modelling I use in my research.</details>
- [Probabilistic Systems Analysis and Applied Probability (6.041), John Tsitsiklis](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-041-probabilistic-systems-analysis-and-applied-probability-fall-2010/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The fuller version, with more problems and inference. Great for thinking clearly about uncertainty and statistical dependence.</details>
- [Discrete Stochastic Processes (6.262)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-262-discrete-stochastic-processes-spring-2011/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Markov chains, renewal processes and martingales: the theory behind sequential data and random processes. Demanding but rewarding.</details>
- [Introduction to Functional Analysis (18.102)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-102-introduction-to-functional-analysis-spring-2021/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Abstract, but Hilbert spaces and operators sit underneath kernel methods, Gaussian processes and signal theory.</details>
- [Nonlinear Programming (15.084J)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-084j-nonlinear-programming-spring-2004/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The optimisation theory behind how models actually get fitted: constraints, convexity and algorithms.</details>

## Computer Science and Machine Learning

- [Programming for the Puzzled (6.S095)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-s095-programming-for-the-puzzled-january-iap-2018/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A short, playful course that teaches algorithmic thinking through puzzles. A fun way into programming ideas.</details>
- [Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (6.001)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-001-structure-and-interpretation-of-computer-programs-spring-2005/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The classic on abstraction and how to think about programs. Slow-burning, but it changes how you write code.</details>
- [Introduction to Computational Thinking (18.S191)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-s191-introduction-to-computational-thinking-fall-2022/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Mixes maths, data and simulation with interactive notebooks. Great for learning by modelling.</details>
- [Introduction to Algorithms (6.006)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A clear treatment of data structures and algorithm analysis. The foundation for writing efficient code.</details>
- [Artificial Intelligence (6.034), Patrick Winston](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-034-artificial-intelligence-fall-2010/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>An intuitive, broad tour of classical AI from before the deep learning era. Good for seeing where today's ideas came from.</details>
- [Introduction to Deep Learning (6.S191)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-s191-introduction-to-deep-learning-january-iap-2020/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A fast, well-paced overview of modern deep learning and its main architectures.</details>
- [Hands-On Deep Learning (15.773)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-773-hands-on-deep-learning-spring-2024/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The practical companion: building and training models in code cements the theory.</details>

## Signals and Systems

- [Signals and Systems (RES.6-007), Alan Oppenheim](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-007-signals-and-systems-spring-2011/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The standard foundation for filtering, Fourier analysis and system response. Essential for any EEG or audio work.</details>
- [Digital Signal Processing (RES.6-008)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-008-digital-signal-processing-spring-2011/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Sampling, discrete transforms and filter design, directly relevant to preprocessing neural and acoustic data.</details>

## Neuroscience and Cognition

- [Philosophical Issues in Brain Science (24.08J)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/24-08j-philosophical-issues-in-brain-science-spring-2009/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Asks what neuroscience can and cannot explain about mind and consciousness. Keeps the conceptual questions in view.</details>
- [Perception (9.35)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/9-35-perception-spring-2024/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>How the brain builds perception, mainly vision and audition. Ties psychophysics to neural mechanisms.</details>
- [Introduction to Neural Computation (9.40)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/9-40-introduction-to-neural-computation-spring-2018/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Models of neurons and networks with hands-on maths. A great bridge between biophysics and computation.</details>
- [Brain and Cognitive Sciences Computational Tutorial Series (RES.9-008)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-9-008-brain-and-cognitive-sciences-computational-tutorials/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Short practical tutorials in data analysis and modelling for neuroscience. Good for learning by doing.</details>
- [Introduction to Computational Neuroscience with Neuroblox (RES.9-009)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-9-009-introduction-to-computational-neuroscience-with-neuroblox-january-iap-2025/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>An introduction to simulating brain circuits with a modern toolbox, linking models to dynamics.</details>
- [Brains, Minds and Machines Summer Course (RES.9-003)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-9-003-brains-minds-and-machines-summer-course-summer-2015/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Talks from leading researchers on how brains and AI relate. Broad and inspiring for the neuro-AI perspective.</details>
- [fMRI Bootcamp (RES.9-005)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-9-005-fmri-bootcamp-fall-2017/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A practical and theoretical overview of fMRI design and analysis. Helps to read the neuroimaging literature critically.</details>
- [AFNI Training Bootcamp (RES.9-006)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-9-006-afni-training-bootcamp-spring-2018/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Hands-on training in a widely used neuroimaging analysis pipeline.</details>

## Biology

- [Fundamentals of Biology (7.01SC)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-01sc-fundamentals-of-biology-fall-2011/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A well-structured entry point to molecular and cell biology, with problem sets that make it stick.</details>
- [Introduction to Biology (7.012)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-012-introduction-to-biology-fall-2004/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Another strong take on the basics, with a different teaching style. Useful as a second pass.</details>
- [Foundations of Computational and Systems Biology (7.91J)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-91j-foundations-of-computational-and-systems-biology-spring-2014/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Applies modelling and computation to biological questions. Good for seeing how quantitative methods meet the life sciences.</details>

## Language, Humanities and Social Science

- [Introduction to Linguistics (24.900)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/24-900-introduction-to-linguistics-spring-2022/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Covers the core of the field, from sounds and structure to meaning. A good complement to my work on prosody.</details>
- [Old English and Beowulf (21L.601J)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/21l-601j-old-english-and-beowulf-spring-2023/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Reading Beowulf in Old English with close attention to language history. A pleasure for anyone who loves philology.</details>
- [Film as Visual and Literary Mythmaking (24.264)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/24-264-film-as-visual-and-literary-mythmaking-fall-2005/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Looks at how film retells myth. A nice change of pace from the technical courses.</details>
- [Data Analysis for Social Scientists (14.310x)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/14-310x-data-analysis-for-social-scientists-spring-2023/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Practical statistics and data analysis, with an emphasis on drawing sound conclusions from messy data.</details>
